12 Initial Test Program


PSAR chapter 12, “Initial Test Program,” describes the initial test program (ITP) that is
performed during the initial startup of the Long Mott Generating Station (LMGS).

The applicable regulatory requirements for the evaluation of the ITP are as follows:

   •   Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 50.34(a)(7)
   •   Criterion XI, “Test Control,” of Appendix B to 10 CFR Part 50

The NRC staff has issued the following guidance for the development and review of the post-
construction inspection, testing, and analysis program (PITAP):

   •   DANU-ISG-2022-06, “Advanced Reactor Content of Application Project, Chapter 12
       ‘Post-manufacturing and construction Inspection, Testing, and Analysis Program,’”
       (ML23277A144).

12.1 Technical Evaluation


The NRC staff reviewed the LMGS ITP against the criteria provided in DANU-ISG-2022-06. For
a CP application, DANU-ISG-2022-06 states that the PITAP description can be limited to the
preoperational phase inspection, testing, and verification that would be required by 10 CFR Part
50, Appendix B, and that the PITAP should include a description of the scope, objectives, and
programmatic controls associated with the preoperational test program (prior to initial fuel
loading). Accordingly, the NRC staff’s review, as presented below, is limited to the: (1) scope,
(2) objectives, and (3) programmatic controls for Phase 1 of the LMGS ITP (i.e., preoperational
inspection, testing, and verification).

12.1.1 Scope
The NRC staff evaluated the structures, systems, and components (SSCs) included in the
scope of the LMGS ITP cold commissioning and preoperational testing consistent with DANU-
ISG-2022-06, Section F, “Acceptance Criteria,” which states that the preoperational inspection,
testing, and verification program (including elements of the quality assurance program, as
applicable) includes all SR and safety-significant SSCs that can reasonably be verified at the
preoperational stage.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR section 5.1, which states, “Safety-significant SSCs include all
those SSCs classified as SR [safety-related] or NSRST [non-safety-related with special
treatment].” PSAR section 12.1.1 describes the commissioning process and states that the
scope of the initial test program addresses all safety-significant SSCs.

The NRC staff determined that the description of the scope provided in the PSAR is consistent
with DANU-ISG-2022-06 and therefore acceptable because the initial test program addresses
all safety-significant SSCs, which includes all SSCs classified as SR or NSRST.

12.1.2 Objectives
The NRC staff reviewed the ITP objectives consistent with DANU-ISG-2022-06, which
states that the primary objective of the PITAP is to demonstrate, to the extent possible,
that the safety-significant SSCs as constructed or manufactured, as the case may be,
will operate in accordance with the design and as described in the safety analysis report.

DANU-ISG-2022-06 also states that additional objectives of the PITAP for preoperational
testing include:

   •   providing reasonable assurance that the facility exhibits the performance and associated
       safety margins described in the design
   •   satisfying any license conditions associated with the PITAP
   •   obtaining as-built data to verify the analytical assumptions, limits, and models
   •   familiarizing the plant’s operating and technical staff with operation of the facility
   •   verifying the adequacy of the plant operating and emergency procedures

The NRC staff did consider objectives in DANU-ISG-2022-06 that are not applicable to
CP applications.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR section 12.1.1, which states that “[t]he objective of the
commissioning strategy is to demonstrate that the plant as constructed meets the design
and safety requirements specified in the Final Safety Analysis Report (FSAR), license
conditions, Technical Specifications (TS), and as specified in the requirements
management program through corresponding acceptance criteria.” To accomplish this,
PSAR section 12.1.1 also states that the LMGS ITP includes:

   •   Verification that safety-significant SSCs fulfill design and safety requirements through
       attainment of corresponding acceptance criteria
   •   Measurement and collection of plant operating data for SSCs and integrated plant
       responses for validation of analyses and future reference as well as to validate any
       applicable analytical assumptions, limits, or models
   •   Validation that all operating, surveillance, and emergency procedures are adequate
   •   Demonstration of operating staff proficiency and, that maintenance and technical staff
       have the required skills and abilities to fulfill their job functions

PSAR chapter 12 also states that the ITP provides assurance that the operating and emergency
procedures have been evaluated and demonstrated, and that the plant operations personnel are
knowledgeable about the plant operating procedures and are fully prepared to operate the plant
in a safe manner.

In PSAR section 12.1.2, LME described the scope of first-of-a-kind (FOAK) SSC testing that will
be performed under the ITP. As stated in PSAR section 12.1.2, the tests are intended to “verify
that safety-significant FOAK SSCs not validated through other verification methods were
constructed and will operate in accordance with their design.” The NRC staff determined that
the preliminary description in PSAR section 12.1.2 meets the acceptance criteria by identifying
and including FOAK SSCs in the ITP.

The NRC staff determined that the PSAR description captures those portions of the ITP
objectives described in DANU-2022-06 that are relevant at the CP stage. Further, nothing about
the differences between the submitted ITP description and the guidance in DANU-ISG-2022-06
necessitates a different or expanded ITP objective. This is because the ITP objectives described
in the PSAR capture what is necessary to meet the applicable regulatory requirements for
issuance of a CP in accordance with 10 CFR 50.34(a) and 10 CFR 50, Appendix B. Therefore,
the NRC staff finds that the objectives of the LMGS ITP are acceptable.

12.1.3 Programmatic Controls
The NRC staff reviewed the ITP cold commissioning testing and preoperational testing
programmatic controls described in the PSAR. PSAR chapter 12 states that the ITP is executed
under the QA program described in the topical report, “Long Mott Energy, LLC Quality
Assurance Program Description” (ML24345A045). The NRC staff’s review of the QA program as
applicable to the ITP is discussed in section 8.1 of this safety evaluation (SE).

Based on the use of an acceptable QA program, as described in section 8.1, “Quality
Assurance” of this SE, and because the LMGS QA program description contains adequate
programmatic controls for the conduct of the ITP, the NRC staff determined that the
programmatic controls for conduct of the LMGS ITP are acceptable.

  12.2 Conclusion

Based on the information above, the NRC staff finds that the ITP is acceptable for addressing
the test control requirement under 10 CFR 50.34(a)(7) and Criterion XI, “Test Control,” of
Appendix B to 10 CFR Part 50.
